Let me analyze this task. I need to estimate software development effort for a software increment described in the specification. The specification is about Spring Cloud Data Flow (s-c-d) — a set of user stories related to the Spring Cloud Data Flow project migrating from Spring XD.

The user stories are:
- U1: Runtime info as shell command (list details about module: host, port, etc.)
- U2: Deploy data flow on YARN (reuse existing Hadoop cluster)
- U3: Port file module from XD to s-c-s (Spring Cloud Stream) repo as source module
- U4: Break build lifecycle to bundle SPI deployers individually
- U5: Get rid of XDRuntimeException from XD
- U6: Use latest release of gemfire sink
- U7: SFTP source module available as OOTB module
- U8: Resolve remaining gaps wrt CI pipelines for Data Flow

I need to:
1. Break down into activities (WBS)
2. State technical/design decisions and assumptions
3. Provide most likely effort per activity
4. Sum total

Output must be valid JSON matching the schema.

Let me think about a WBS. I could structure it per user story, with sub-activities for design, implementation, testing, documentation, integration. Effort in work-hours.

Let me estimate each user story:

U1: Runtime info shell command — implement a new shell command in Spring Cloud Data Flow shell that queries runtime info about deployed modules (host, port, attributes). This corresponds to the "runtime apps" command in SCDF. Effort: maybe 40-60 hours including REST endpoint and shell command, tests.

Actually, the spec says "runtime info as shell command" — need an endpoint on admin (server) that exposes runtime info of deployed stream modules (instances, host, port, attributes), and a shell command that displays it in a table.

U2: Deploy data flow on YARN — implement a Spring Cloud Deployer for YARN. This is a big task: SPI implementation, integration with YARN (submitting apps via YARN client), handling streams and tasks, tests on a cluster, docs. Effort: maybe 200-320 hours.

U3: Port file module from XD to spring-cloud-stream-modules repo as source. Migrate code, refactor to use Spring Cloud Stream binder abstraction instead of XD, update to Spring Boot/Cloud standards, tests, docs. Effort: maybe 40-60 hours.

U4: Break build lifecycle to bundle SPI deployers individually — restructure Maven build so deployers are separate artifacts (local, YARN, CF, kubernetes etc. as separate modules), admin server decoupled. Effort: maybe 60-100 hours.

U5: Remove XDRuntimeException from XD — refactoring to remove the exception class and use standard exceptions; lots of code references. Effort: maybe 24-40 hours. Actually "get rid of XDRuntimeException from XD" — this is in XD codebase, refactoring. Since XD is legacy, maybe this is about removing dependency in migration. Effort: 16-32 hours.

U6: Latest release of gemfire sink — update gemfire sink module to latest gemfire release, resolve API changes, tests, release. Effort: maybe 24-40 hours.

U7: SFTP source module — create SFTP source as OOTB module and publish to maven repo. SFTP source existed in XD; need to port/create new module based on Spring Integration SFTP inbound adapter. Effort: maybe 40-60 hours.

U8: CI pipeline gaps for Data Flow and family — set up/complete Jenkins/Concourse pipelines for build, test, release of SCDF, deployers, stream/task modules. Effort: maybe 60-100 hours.

Plus cross-cutting activities: overall design/architecture alignment, integration testing, release management, documentation.

Let me structure the WBS with activities per story, each possibly broken into analysis/design, implementation, testing. But the schema wants a flat list of activities with IDs. I can include sub-activities with hierarchical IDs like "U1.1".

Let me think about reasonable total. These stories come from real Spring Cloud Data Flow early days (2015-2016). Total effort maybe ~700-900 hours.

Let me define activities:

A1 (U1): Runtime info shell command
- A1.1 Design REST API and shell command UX: 8h
- A1.2 Implement server-side runtime info endpoint (aggregate deployed module instance info: host, port, attributes from deployer SPI): 24h
- A1.3 Implement shell command with tabular rendering: 12h
- A1.4 Unit + integration tests: 16h
- A1.5 Docs: 4h
Subtotal: 64h

A2 (U2): YARN deployer
- A2.1 Design/architecture for YARN deployer SPI: 16h
- A2.2 Implement YARN deployer (app submission, status, undeploy) for stream modules: 80h
- A2.3 Support task/batch deployments on YARN: 40h
- A2.4 Integration tests on Hadoop cluster: 48h
- A2.5 Docs and samples: 16h
Subtotal: 200h

A3 (U3): File source port
- A3.1 Port module code from XD to spring-cloud-stream-modules structure (Boot autoconfigure, binder): 20h
- A3.2 Unit + integration tests: 12h
- A3.3 Docs + release to maven repo: 8h
Subtotal: 40h

A4 (U4): Build lifecycle restructure
- A4.1 Design multi-module build structure for deployer SPI artifacts: 12h
- A4.2 Refactor Maven poms; admin server decoupled from deployer implementations; generate individual deployer bundles: 32h
- A4.3 Verify builds and dependency convergence; update distribution packaging: 16h
Subtotal: 60h

A5 (U5): Remove XDRuntimeException
- A5.1 Inventory usages, define replacement strategy (standard exceptions / new exception hierarchy): 8h
- A5.2 Refactor code and tests: 16h
Subtotal: 24h

A6 (U6): Gemfire sink update
- A6.1 Upgrade gemfire dependency to latest release; adapt to API changes: 16h
- A6.2 Tests (unit/integration with gemfire): 12h
- A6.3 Release/publish: 4h
Subtotal: 32h

A7 (U7): SFTP source
- A7.1 Implement SFTP source module (Spring Integration SFTP inbound, session factory config, properties): 24h
- A7.2 Unit + integration tests (embedded SFTP server): 16h
- A7.3 Register as OOTB module; publish bits to repo.spring.io; docs: 12h
Subtotal: 52h

A8 (U8): CI pipelines
- A8.1 Assess gaps and design pipeline plan: 8h
- A8.2 Implement build/test pipelines for SCDF, deployers, stream modules, task modules: 40h
- A8.3 Release/promotion pipeline automation: 24h
- A8.4 Validation on every commit, flaky test fixes: 16h
Subtotal: 88h

A9: Cross-cutting integration & release
- A9.1 End-to-end integration testing across stories (e.g., SFTP/file/gemfire in streams deployed on YARN via SCDF): 32h
- A9.2 Overall documentation/release notes: 12h
Subtotal: 44h

technical_and_design_decisions: U1: Expose runtime module details (host, port, and other instance attributes) via a new REST endpoint on the Data Flow (admin) server that aggregates instance data from the deployer SPI, and add a corresponding shell command that renders the result as a table.

U2: Implement the YARN support as a new spring-cloud-deployer implementation (AppDeployer and TaskLauncher SPIs) built on the Spring for Apache Hadoop YARN client, running stream/task apps as YARN containers using a cluster-accessible binder (e.g., Kafka).

U3: Port the file module into the spring-cloud-stream-modules repository as a Spring Boot auto-configured application using @EnableBinding(Source), replacing the legacy XD transport with the Spring Cloud Stream binder abstraction.

U4: Restructure the Maven build so each SPI deployer (local, YARN, etc.) is built and published as an individual artifact; the admin server depends only on the deployer SPI, with the concrete deployer selected at runtime/packaging time.
U5: Remove XDRuntimeException via a mechanical refactoring to a small, well-defined runtime exception hierarchy (or standard exceptions), keeping public API behavior unchanged.
U6: Upgrade the gemfire sink to the latest GemFire release, adapting to changed client/region APIs and updating its integration tests accordingly.

U7: Implement the SFTP source using the Spring Integration SFTP inbound channel adapter with a configurable session factory; test against an embedded Apache MINA SSHD server; register it as an out-of-the-box module and publish bits to repo.spring.io.
U8: Close CI gaps with per-commit build/test pipelines plus a release/promotion pipeline covering Data Flow, deployers, and stream/task module repositories.
All new modules follow the existing project conventions (Spring Boot auto-configuration, Maven, JUnit/Integration tests) and are documented in the reference docs.
assumptions: The placeholder tokens in the stories are interpreted from context: {{runtime info}} = runtime instance information command, {{host}}/{{port}} = instance attributes, {{file}} = file module, {{source}} = Spring Cloud Stream source, {{admin}} = Data Flow admin server, {{XDRuntimeException}} = legacy Spring XD exception, {{gemfire}} = GemFire sink module, {{module list}} = OOTB module listing page.

activities.activity_description: Refine the eight user stories, confirm scope boundaries, and align the technical approach (deployer SPI usage, module porting conventions, build restructure impact) before implementation.

activities.activity_name: Design runtime-info API and shell UX
activities.activity_description: Define the REST resource shape (instances with host, port, and attributes) and the shell command output format.
Implement the Data Flow server endpoint that aggregates deployed module instance details (host, port, attributes) from the deployer SPI.
Add the shell command that invokes the endpoint and renders module runtime details as a table.
Cover endpoint aggregation logic and shell command rendering with unit and integration tests.
Update the shell and REST API reference documentation for the new runtime info command.

activities.activity_name: YARN deployer architecture and SPI design
activities.activity_description: Design how AppDeployer/TaskLauncher SPIs map to YARN submission, status, and undeploy operations using the existing Hadoop client stack.
Implement deployment, status, scaling, and undeployment of stream modules as YARN containers.
Implement launching of batch/task workloads on YARN with status and cleanup support.
Verify stream and task deployments end-to-end on a real Hadoop/YARN cluster.
Write getting-started documentation and a working sample for running Data Flow on YARN.
Migrate the file module from XD to the stream modules repo as a Boot auto-configured source using the binder abstraction.
Add unit and integration tests for the ported file source module.
Document the module options and publish the artifact to the repository.
Define the target multi-module build layout so each SPI deployer is bundled and released individually.

activities.activity_name: Refactor build for individual deployer bundles
activities.activity_description: Rework Maven POMs so deployers are separate artifacts and the admin server is decoupled from specific deployer implementations.
Verify dependency convergence, adjust distribution packaging, and confirm all deployer variants build independently.

activities.activity_name: XDRuntimeException usage inventory and replacement strategy
activities.activity_description: Locate all usages in the XD codebase and define the replacement exception strategy.
Perform the refactoring across code and tests, removing the exception type entirely.

activities.activity_name: Upgrade gemfire sink to latest release
activities.activity_description: Bump the GemFire dependency and adapt the sink to changed APIs.
Update and extend unit/integration tests against the new GemFire version.
Publish the updated sink module artifact.
Create the SFTP source based on the Spring Integration SFTP inbound adapter with configurable session factory and module properties.
Add unit and integration tests using an embedded SFTP (SSHD) server.
Register SFTP as an out-of-the-box module in the module list and publish its bits to the Maven snapshot repository; document usage.

activities.activity_name: CI gap assessment and pipeline plan
activities.activity_description: Assess remaining CI gaps across Data Flow and related repositories and define the pipeline plan.
Create per-commit build/test pipelines for Data Flow, deployers, and stream/task module repositories.
Automate release and promotion stages so every commit can be continuously evaluated and artifacts promoted.
Fix flaky tests and validate that every commit triggers full functional evaluation.
Verify the increment as a whole: build streams using the file, SFTP, and gemfire modules, deploy them via Data Flow on local and YARN, and check runtime info reporting.
Prepare consolidated release notes and final documentation pass for the increment.
